key_insight: UNSM changed the local hardness of Cr3C2–NiCr coatings in a sample-dependent way, with detonation-sprayed coatings showing 820–970 HV and HVOF coatings spanning a broader 546–1165 HV range.
engineering_relevance: The study helps compare how deposition route and surface modification affect near-surface mechanical performance and post-scratch integrity in wear-resistant coatings.
method: Detonation-sprayed (DS) and HVOF Cr3C2–NiCr coatings were treated by ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM).
Scratch tests were performed at 20 and 30 N with 20 and 30 µm vibration amplitudes.
Instrumental hardness was measured at 300 mN load with a 10 s dwell time.
evidence_signal: SEM after scratching showed heterogeneous contrast and crack-like discontinuities in both coating series, while reported hardness values varied strongly by sample and treatment condition.
watch_item: The post-scratch SEM observations are qualitative and do not isolate damage specifically caused by UNSM, so they should not be used alone to rank scratch resistance.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
